problem: Existing VLN benchmarks rely on static one-shot instructions, decouple high-level planning from social intention modeling, and their simulators lack dynamic pedestrians, vehicles and socially grounded human-agent interaction.
motivation: Real-world embodied agents must ask people for help, self-assess and adapt to new information in dynamic human-populated scenes. LLMs make it possible to simulate human-like behaviors and instructions, but this has not been connected to closed-loop embodied navigation. The paper argues that interaction itself is an information modality.
key_idea: Build an LLM-driven, closed-loop Unity simulator with realistic human avatars and a Direction Inquiry task, in which the agent asks nearby pedestrians for directions, plus a synthetic dataset for training and evaluating such interactive navigation.
insight: The human baseline shows interaction gives a large gain: allowing questions raises SR from 40.2 to 82.6 and cuts NE from 18.3 to 3.49, so asking is valuable information. Fine-tuning ETPNav/BEVBert on the data reduces open-loop L2 by about 50% and slightly improves closed-loop NE/ONE. Yet closed-loop SR stays 0 for all models, so current VLN models are far from handling dynamic social navigation and inquiry. The models never ask (NDI = 0), so they do not exploit interaction.
method: People Simulation: LLM generates character profiles and daily schedules; a hierarchical planner (high-level schedule, middle-level FSM subtasks, low-level A* + Social Force Model) drives pedestrians

Navigation Style Generation: a knowledge base of wayfinding-language findings (landmark use, direction type, distance description, utterance length) conditions the LLM to generate persona-specific directions
Avatars/Animation/Appearance: SMPL-X with the MotionX animation library, blending, MLLM-guided UV texture generation, shape variation and Synbody assets
System functions: voxel-based 2D occupancy heatmaps, dynamic weather/day-night, route-graph traffic simulation, robot simulation with A*+SFM, WebSocket-based synchronous closed-loop interface
Direction Inquiry Task: VLN extended with an inquiry phase where the agent asks humans for guidance; adds the NDI metric alongside TL, SR, SPL, NE, OSR, ONE

FreeAskWorld Dataset: Unity Perception data collected by an agent that asks pedestrians and navigates with a rule-based planner (six 90° cameras at 1 Hz, RGB, depth, segmentation, boxes, dialogs, trajectories, occupancy) with 16 object categories, 63,429 frames, 17+ hours of data

setting.backbone: ETPNav and BEVBert (original pretrained and fine-tuned on FreeAskWorld); human participants as reference
setting.training_data: Pretrained VLN-CE checkpoints fine-tuned on the FreeAskWorld synthetic dataset (63,429 frames, 17+ hours; the intro says over six hours)
setting.observation: Six 90° RGB cameras forming a panorama at 1 Hz, plus depth and other synthetic annotations, with dialog/instruction text
setting.action_space: Continuous low-level control via the simulator (rotate-then-forward for ETPNav), 1 Hz update, plus an inquiry action for asking humans
setting.privileged: none for the models; the data-collection agent uses a rule-based expert planner

numbers.extra: closed-loop in simulator; 100-step limit, terminates on collision; no inquiry (NDI 0)

numbers_note: Open-loop L2 results are only described in text (~50% L2 reduction after fine-tuning) with no table numbers. The human baseline rows (Human ask: SR 82.6, SPL 71.2, NE 3.49; Human no ask: SR 40.2) are reference values, not own-method numbers. The split name is not stated in the paper; 'test' is assumed.
results: In closed-loop evaluation, humans reach SR 82.6 when allowed to ask (NDI 0.78) versus 40.2 when not. All VLN models (ETPNav, BEVBert, and their fine-tuned versions) have SR 0; fine-tuning only improves NE/ONE slightly, and ETPNav-FT is the only model with nonzero OSR (1.1). In open-loop evaluation, fine-tuned models roughly halve L2 error, with BEVBert-FT best.
limitations: Fine-tuned models still fail completely (SR 0) in closed loop and never use inquiry (NDI 0), so the evaluation does not test asking behavior
Only two older VLN baselines and a small human study (4 participants) are evaluated; the dataset is fully synthetic with rule-based expert trajectories
Only the direction-inquiry interaction is implemented, and the paper gives limited quantitative detail (open-loop numbers are not tabulated)
